title: Bonito Winter Festival Energizes the Cultural Scene
seoTitle: Bonito Winter Festival Energizes Cultural Scene
subtitle: With a diverse program, the event attracts audiences of all ages and puts the topic “festival” in the spotlight.
excerpt: The Bonito Winter Festival stands out in Brazil’s cultural landscape with a wide program that includes music, theater, dance, literature and gastronomy.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Brazilian cultural scene shines with the vibrancy of events that animate cities and attract audiences of all ages. This weekend, the Bonito Winter Festival, with a diversified schedule that runs through Sunday, July 30, is one of the main catalysts for the growing interest in festivals across the country.

Bonito Winter Festival in the Spotlight

The city of Bonito has become the stage for an extensive cultural agenda that began on the morning of Friday, July 28, and continues until Sunday, July 30. The program spreads across different spots in the city and covers music, theater, dance, literature, gastronomy, handicrafts and activities aimed at children.

Among the many options, visitors can wander through craft, fashion and creative‑economy spaces at Praça da Liberdade throughout the day. There is also a Geek‑Literary Lounge with an open gaming area and talks, as well as performing‑arts shows that make up the night agenda.

Attractions for All Ages

The festival aims to bring generations together, offering activities that please both kids and adults. The "Turma da Boiadeirinha" troupe, for example, brought music and fun to the children’s audience on the afternoon of Friday, July 28, at the Lua Stage. For parents, the attraction became an opportunity to share an experience with their kids, and for some families it was their first time at an event of this kind.

For adult audiences, the musical program stretches across several stages, with shows that blend different genres and promise to enliven the festival nights. The diversity seeks to ensure that every participant finds something of interest over the days of the event.

Music and Pedagogy for the Little Ones

One of the highlights of the children’s schedule was the performance by Turma da Boiadeirinha, a character inspired by singer Ana Castela. The animated series, also drawing inspiration from Luan Pereira, relies on music and education to create a universe for kids. With original songs and a pedagogical approach, the production promotes values such as respect, empathy and learning.

Mothers like Elizete Rosa and Edilaine Nunes Pereira took their children to watch the show. Elizete said her daughters already knew Turma da Boiadeirinha from the internet and are fans of the songs, making the encounter with the characters a special experience. Edilaine shared her son’s excitement—he loves music and enjoys singing—living his first festival experience. She added, “I’m totally ‘into it’; I like what he likes, right? I get excited for him to see it and he’s loving it.” The troupe’s goal is precisely to create moments of exchange and memories between parents and children.

Diverse Musical Line‑up

Music took center stage at the Bonito Winter Festival. On the night of Friday, July 28, singer Léo Foguete took the Lua Stage, cementing his status as one of the breakout artists on digital platforms with his blend of piseiro, forró and sertanejo. Before him, the evening featured DJ PK and the group Forrodiando o Forró do MS.

The Friday afternoon musical schedule also included performances such as Sexteto D’Sete on the Sesc Estrela Stage, and on the Sol Stage, Wandersom Fonseca, Álvaro Cesar Trio, Brass & Beats Sextet and Grupo Festeiros do MS. For the following days, Seu Jorge is confirmed for Saturday, July 29, with a repertoire that mixes samba, soul, Brazilian Popular Music (MPB) and funk, and the duo Humberto & Ronaldo will close the festival on Sunday, July 30, with hits from university sertanejo.

Other Cultural Options

Beyond music, the Bonito Winter Festival offers a range of cultural activities. At Praça da Liberdade, the audience could follow the Fantastic Playful Parade and the Parade of Authorial Brands of Mato Grosso do Sul. In the Geek‑Literary Lounge, Sarah Muricy presented the talk “Who Are Our Celebrities?”.

The performing arts also had their space on the Sol Stage, with Grupo Casa presenting “The Great Little Things of the Pantanal”, followed by a show by Kelly Lopes and the performance “I Love You” by the Sesc MS Dance Company. The variety of events ensures the festival is a meeting point for diverse artistic and cultural expressions.

Information from G1, Campo Grande News.
